g.text: One France→China swap redirects the whole country — and selectivity arrives with scale

text.style: font-size: 10.5px; font-family: '-apple-system', 'Segoe UI', 'Helvetica Neue', 'Arial', 'DejaVu Sans', 'Bitstream Vera Sans', 'Computer Modern Sans Serif', 'Lucida Grande', 'Verdana', 'Geneva', 'Lucid', 'Helvetica', 'Avant Garde', sans-serif; text-anchor: start; fill: #52514e

g.text: Swap the France and China J-vectors on the mid-network band; read four downstream facts + a Germany control.

text.style: font-size: 8px; font-family: '-apple-system', 'Segoe UI', 'Helvetica Neue', 'Arial', 'DejaVu Sans', 'Bitstream Vera Sans', 'Computer Modern Sans Serif', 'Lucida Grande', 'Verdana', 'Geneva', 'Lucid', 'Helvetica', 'Avant Garde', sans-serif; text-anchor: start; fill: #898781

g.text: The shaded row is the selectivity control (Germany’s capital). On 1.5B, “Beijing” leaks into it (0.06) — the patch is a sledgehammer; on 7B it stays out (0.01). Source: scripts/france_china.py
